C1.name: Founder-market fit
C1.covers: Earned secrets, time in the field. Pedigree alone scores 0.

C3.name: Customer pull
C3.covers: Repeat, conversion, groundwork. Not raw size.

C4.name: Numbers fluency
C4.covers: Cohorts, CAC by channel, figures that reconcile.

C5.name: Pre-seed fit
C5.covers: Capital intensity, valuation, path to the next round.

C6.name: Why now and copy risk
C6.covers: What changed, and the answer to a well-funded copier.

C1.0: Pedigree only; no time in this market.
C1.3: Adjacent experience; learned the problem second-hand.
C1.5: Some years near the customer; one earned insight.
C1.7: Years in the field; names a non-obvious truth with evidence.
C1.10: Lived the problem for years and built the first version on that knowledge (Tadka Ghar, Dukaan Dost).

C2.0: Pushes the hardest risk onto a partner (QuickPaisa: defaults are the NBFC's problem).
C2.3: Aware of the risk; no plan.
C2.7: Owns the risk with data from the field.
C2.10: Did groundwork before lending or building; owns losses (Mitti Credit).

C3.7: Repeat by cohort holding above sector norm.
C3.10: Cohort curves flatten high; customers pull the product (Boli Seekho, 34% M6).

C4.3: Totals only; can't split by channel.
C4.7: CAC by channel, margins and cohorts that reconcile.
C4.10: Knows every number and why it moved (Tadka Ghar).

C5.0: Needs far more capital than a pre-seed cheque before proof (Charge Chalo).
C5.7: Clear milestones the cheque can reach.
C5.10: Capital-light, fair price, clear next-round proof.

C6.0: Depends on a rule change going its way (Chainmandi), or defensive about copiers (Ledgerline).
C6.5: A real shift, weak answer to copiers.
C6.7: Specific shift and a credible moat.
C6.10: Earned timing plus a structural answer to a well-funded copier (Pervalent milestones).
